claim: The default documented active-passive HA leader-election mechanism for llm-d-router EPP replicas requires the Kubernetes API server via a coordination.k8s.io/Lease object.
stance_target: existence of a Kubernetes-independent leader-election path for the default active-passive HA mode
scope_conditions: llm-d-router EPP, active-passive HA mode, router.epp.replicas > 1, no priority routing
quoted_support: In multi-replica deployments without priority routing (router.epp.replicas > 1), the router coordinates active-passive replicas using Kubernetes lease-based leader election: EPP replicas contend for a coordination.k8s.io/Lease. The --ha-enable-leader-election flag enables leader election in EPP (automatically injected by Helm when router.epp.replicas > 1). The elected leader responds to active gRPC extension requests on Port 9002, while standby replicas run idle.

claim: No file-based, static-peer-list, or gossip-based alternative to the Kubernetes Lease is documented for EPP active-passive leader election in llm-d-router.
stance_target: existence of a non-Kubernetes lock/lease primitive for EPP leader election
quoted_support: Leader Election with Fail-Open: Uses Kubernetes coordination.k8s.io/Lease coordination so only the elected leader serves inference extension requests. Standby pods remain idle until acquiring the lease.

claim: The only documented ways to avoid the Kubernetes Lease dependency are to disable leader election entirely (running Fully Active-Active) or to substitute a different Kubernetes-native mechanism (StatefulSet + headless Service + Envoy Outlier Detection/health checks via Priority Routing), not a non-Kubernetes lock.
stance_target: whether any HA path in llm-d-router avoids Kubernetes entirely
scope_conditions: llm-d-router HA modes: Fully Active-Active, Active-Passive with Priority Routing, Active-Passive with Leader Election
quoted_support: Deterministic Endpoint Discovery: EPP pods run as a StatefulSet with a headless Service (publishNotReadyAddresses: true). Envoy targets individual pod DNS entries... Outlier Detection Failover: ...Envoy's Outlier Detection detects TCP connection failure and ejects the primary host, shifting traffic to Priority 1 standbys in sub-second time without lease expiration delays.

claim: Active-Active EPP mode is enabled by explicitly setting ha-enable-leader-election to false, avoiding the Kubernetes Lease dependency but sacrificing shared prefix-cache state across replicas.
stance_target: existence of a Kubernetes-lease-free EPP HA mode
quoted_support: To run multi-replica in Fully Active-Active mode instead, set router.epp.flags.ha-enable-leader-election: false. ... Active-Active mode should be avoided when using approximate prefix routing. Because EPP replicas do not share prefix state, each replica only has visibility into the prefix state of the requests it has individually handled.

claim: Active-Active EPP mode provides near-linear but sub-linear throughput scaling: 2 replicas = 2.0x, 3 replicas = 2.7x, 4 replicas = 3.5x.
scope_conditions: llm-d-router EPP Active-Active mode, benchmark data from linked Issue #1290
quoted_support: Active-Active Mode: Multiple EPP replicas actively share and load-balance incoming requests, providing near-linear throughput scaling: | 1 | 1.0x | | 2 | 2.0x | | 3 | 2.7x | | 4 | 3.5x |

claim: Fail-open behavior during Lease-based leader election means the proxy routes traffic directly to model servers (bypassing the EPP scheduler entirely) while a standby replica is acquiring the lease.
stance_target: failure-mode behavior of Kubernetes-lease-based leader election
scope_conditions: llm-d-router, router.proxy.failOpen: true (standalone mode default) or InferencePool failureMode FailOpen
quoted_support: Fail-Open Resiliency: With router.proxy.failOpen: true (the default in standalone mode) or router.inferencePool.failureMode: FailOpen, if the active leader crashes or restarts, the proxy passes requests directly to backend model servers without dropping traffic during the lease transition period.
